([[Brownsville, Tennessee]]) | college = * [[Kennesaw State Owls men's basketball|Kennesaw State]] (2017–2018) * [[Three Rivers College (Missouri)|Three Rivers]] (2018–2019) * [[Jackson State Tigers basketball|Jackson State]] (2019–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[Southwestern Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SWAC Player of the Year]] (2021) * First-team All-[[Southwestern Athletic Conference|SWAC]] (2021) * Second-team All-SWAC (2020) }} '''Tristan Jarrett''' (born August 6, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kennesaw State Owls men's basketball|Kennesaw State Owls]], the [[Three Rivers College (Missouri)|Three Rivers Raiders]], and the [[Jackson State Tigers basketball|Jackson State Tigers]]. ==High school career== Jarrett attended [[Haywood High School]] in [[Brownsville, Tennessee]]. As a senior, he averaged 21.8 points and 8.6 rebounds per game, leading his team to a Region 8-AA championship. Jarrett was named All-West Tennessee Player of the Year by ''[[The Jackson Sun]]''.{{cite web |last1=Odom |first1=Michael |title=Haywood's Jarrett named Boys Hoops Player of the Year |url=https://www.jacksonsun.com/story/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/2017/04/29/haywoods-jarrett-named-boys-hoops-player-year/100962950/ |website=[[The Jackson Sun]] |access-date=March 4, 2021 |date=April 29, 2017}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Kennesaw State Owls men's basketball|Kennesaw State]] over scholarship offers from [[Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders men's basketball|Middle Tennessee]], [[Little Rock Trojans men's basketball|Little Rock]] and [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State]].{{cite web |last1=Odom |first1=Michael |title=Haywood's Tristan Jarrett signs with Kennesaw State |url=https://www.jacksonsun.com/story/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/2017/05/15/haywoods-tristan-jarrett-signs-kennesaw-state/321780001/ |website=[[The Jackson Sun]] |access-date=March 4, 2021 |date=May 15, 2017}} He was considered a three-star recruit by [[ESPN]].{{cite web |last1=Fields |first1=Nate |title=Tristan Jarrett is reaping the benefits of his move to Three Rivers |url=http://www.raidersathletics.com/sports/mbkb/2018-19/releases/Tristan_Jarrett_is_reaping_the_benefits_of_his_move_to_Three_Rivers |website=Three Rivers College |access-date=March 4, 2021 |date=January 12, 2019}} ==College career== Jarrett averaged 4.8 points through 12 games at Kennesaw State before leaving the program.{{cite web |last1=Flynn |first1=Bryan |title=Tristan Jarrett |url=https://www.jacksonfreepress.com/news/2020/nov/19/tristan-jarrett/ |website=[[Jackson Free Press]] |access-date=March 4, 2021 |date=November 19, 2020}} He moved to [[Three Rivers College (Missouri)|Three Rivers College]], where he averaged 29 points as a sophomore and led his team in five statistical categories. He was dismissed from the program for violating team rules. For his junior season, Jarrett transferred to [[Jackson State Tigers basketball|Jackson State]].{{cite web |last1=Mauro |first1=Bryan |title=SWAC Basketball: In-depth look at Jackson State senior guard Tristan Jarrett |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2020/10/16/swac-basketball-depth-look-jackson-state-senior-guard-tristan-jarrett/ |website=Busting Brackets |access-date=March 4, 2021 |date=October 16, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 16.8 points and 3.4 rebounds per game, earning Second Team All-[[Southwestern Athletic Conference]] (SWAC) recognition.{{cite web |title=Jackson State's Jarrett and McKinnis awarded SWAC basketball preseason honors, all-conference teams announced |url=https://hbcusports.com/2020/11/03/jackson-states-jarrett-and-mckinnis-awarded-swac-basketball-preseason-honors-all-conference-teams-announced/ |website=HBCU Sports |access-date=March 4, 2021 |date=November 3, 2020}} During a game against [[Southern Jaguars basketball|Southern]] on February 8, 2021, Jarrett walked off the court and threw his jersey on his way to the locker room after an argument with teammate Jayveous McKinnis.{{cite web |last1=Gaither |first1=Steven J. |title=Jackson State guard making most of second chance |url=https://hbcugameday.com/2021/03/02/jackson-state-guard-making-most-of-second-chance/ |website=HBCU Gameday |access-date=March 4, 2021 |date=March 2, 2021}} At the close of the regular season, Jarrett was named [[Southwestern Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SWAC Player of the Year]].{{cite press release|url=https://swac.org/news/2021/3/9/swac-announces-mens-basketball-postseason-honors.aspx|title=SWAC Announces Men's Basketball Postseason Honors|publisher=[[Southwestern Athletic Conference]] |date=March 9, 2021 |access-date=March 9, 2021}} He averaged 21.1 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 1.4 steals per game. Following the season, Jarrett declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=Jackson State’s Tristan Jarrett Declares for the 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://hbcugameday.com/2021/04/26/jackson-states-tristan-jarrett-declares-for-the-2021-nba-draft/ |website=HBCU Gameday |access-date=September 25, 2021 |date=April 26, 2021}} ==Professional career== Jarrett was drafted with the 7th pick in the third round of the [[2021 NBA G League draft|2021 NBA G League Draft]] by the [[Raptors 905]].{{Cite web|title=2021 NBA G League Draft Board|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2021-nba-g-league-draft-order/|access-date=2021-10-23|website=NBA G League|language=en-US}} He was waived before the season.{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Blake |title=Raptors 905: 10 storylines to follow for 2021-22 G League season |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-905-10-storylines-follow-2021-22-g-league-season/ |access-date=November 14,
